assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly influential account of how technology and trade shocks reshape labour demand, local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson provide a coherent and recognizable core for the empirical and conceptual contribution.
assessment.maturity: The findings and research agenda have been extensively tested and have strongly shaped policy and subsequent labour research.
uncertainties: The relative weight to place on technology versus trade within one prize citation requires careful framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and made its geographic and policy relevance visible.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central to the linked data and mobility research programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated a mature literature, broad public relevance and replication and extension across settings.
uncertainties: It remains difficult to separate a prize-worthy methodological transformation from the substantive mobility findings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods made credible analysis of persistent economic outcomes feasible in a wide range of empirical settings.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond are the natural core contributors to the principal estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: These methods are long established, widely used and supported by a substantial methodological literature.
uncertainties: Practical misuse and finite-sample weaknesses complicate assessment of the methods' applied legacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has changed how economists understand wage setting and employer power in labour markets.
assessment.attribution: Manning supplied a foundational analytical framework, while Naidu is a leading contributor to its empirical development.
assessment.maturity: The agenda is now central to labour economics and has substantial consequences for competition and wage policy.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping joins foundational theory with a still-evolving empirical literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs gave discrimination research unusually direct and persuasive empirical evidence.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are especially closely identified with the landmark modern audit-study contribution.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively adopted across labour, housing and product markets and has enduring policy significance.
uncertainties: The scope for generalizing measured callback discrimination to later labour-market outcomes remains limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions established the long-run economic importance of child health and skill formation.
assessment.attribution: Almond, Cunha and Currie represent complementary empirical and theoretical foundations of this influential programme.
assessment.maturity: Decades of research across countries support the central importance of early environments.
uncertainties: The broad agenda contains several distinct mechanisms, making a single tightly attributable discovery challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made transparent what data can and cannot establish under credible, limited assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational figure, with Tamer a major contributor to moment-inequality methods.
assessment.maturity: The framework is mature and influential across econometrics and empirical policy analysis.
uncertainties: The contribution is technically broad, and the appropriate boundary between partial identification and related inference advances is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural models of labour supply and household behaviour connected economic theory, tax policy and empirically disciplined counterfactual analysis.
assessment.attribution: Blundell, Meghir and MaCurdy are prominent architects of this research tradition.
assessment.maturity: The work has a long record of methodological influence and policy application.
uncertainties: Structural conclusions can depend materially on modelling assumptions and attribution spans a large literature.
